requirements.gaps: estimated retained caches; original input, temporary work, security auxiliary state and rendering/caller allocations use separate budgets
dependency cycles are errors; excessive acyclic reference depth is a Limit, never a guessed stream length

MediaBox prefers valid CropBox then Letter (612 by 792), a viewing convention also used by PDF.js, not an ISO default; invalid or disjoint CropBox uses MediaBox; resolution and budget errors propagate

Kids order wins over conflicting Parent and Count. Repeated node occurrences are retained in Kids order, bounded by page and traversal-work limits. Cyclic/invalid child edges are omitted only if usable leaves remain. Missing Kids uses explicit typed Parent backlinks in object-number order. Direct dictionaries use their container object identity and distinct page indexes. No identity inferred from inherited attributes or EOF

Limited lexical repairs: bare keys begin with letters and exclude reserved keywords, invalid hash escapes remain literal, object-zero references become null, duplicate opener and one stray parenthesis before dictionary close are reported. Glued endobj needs a proven next object header; direct nested streams remain invalid

Merged offsets pointing to another object header trigger one full reconstruction before lazy loading, never a second retained cache. Nearby corrections retain the existing path; unused entries without recognizable headers remain lazy

Unknown Type needs an xref-selected stream with a validated N/First header; known conflicting roles remain errors. Only a leading self entry aliasing the first real zero offset is discarded; original indexes and a complete physical stream definition are required. Compressed Encrypt/crypt filters and compressed stream Length remain forbidden.

Streams must ordinarily be indirect. Reported recovery keeps dictionaries unchanged and records source paths/ranges in the containing object cache. Payloads use the container encryption identity; direct page contents use the existing stream API. These metadata and header copies are retained-budget charges. A wrong Length needs a unique terminator with a complete dictionary/array continuation. EOF, ambiguous boundaries and duplicate-key scopes containing direct streams are rejected. Direct image resource dictionaries enumerate but drawing them still needs image integration. Direct streams are rejected during security initialization.

EFOpen-only Standard-handler filters are reported as extensions to 7.6.4.1; Identity main-page data may remain readable without an attachment key. Encrypted embedded data still requires credentials. StmF/StrF force DocOpen regardless of AuthEvent contents. CFM None is handler delegation and cannot silently become Identity.

Only missing V=2/R=3 Length is recovered, after the 40-bit default fails and exactly one other legal size authenticates the same supplied credential. Passwords, IDs and other parameters are unchanged. Authentication remains in pagura-crypto; failed or ambiguous trials preserve the original error, and Limit errors propagate.

Only a complete, explicitly typed plaintext Catalog numbered zero is recovered at the exact positive trailer Root xref offset. A matching nearby positive header takes precedence. Generation, Pages reference, endobj and absence of stream payloads are required. Other roles, arbitrary renumbering and encrypted object-key guesses are rejected. No second object slot or retained copy is created.

Identity shadows are ignored before resolving their values. StmF/StrF ignore AuthEvent entirely. V=4 defaults to 128 bits. CF Type, missing required Length, nonstandard Standard-handler names and EFOpen-only extensions are reported deviations; Table 25 with EC3 issue 184 expresses Standard AES lengths in bytes. CFM None delegates to the handler, whose unspecified Standard cipher is explicitly Unsupported rather than Identity.

EncryptMetadata applies only to V=4/5 and only to the catalog-referenced document-level Metadata stream. Object-level Metadata still decrypts. The catalog identity is checked lazily after handler initialization, outside cache publication locks.

Malformed required IDs are reported, not synthesized or padded. The first legacy identifier bytes remain unchanged for hashing; absent/unusable legacy key material is still an error. R5/R6 authentication does not consume IDs, so malformed IDs can be reported without affecting its authenticated key.

Password authentication and Algorithm 13 consistency remain separate. Inconsistent causes a strict security.perms-mismatch error or an explicit repair diagnostic; dictionary permission bytes remain unchanged and malformed security lengths still fail.

An explicit crypto compatibility API authenticates short R4 keys while normal authentication keeps fixed-size checks. Zero-padded object derivation is selected only with a complete zlib checksum and xref-matching object directory, before encrypted objects/strings are cached. Only the first physical xref-selected Flate object stream is probed; no string-only or rebuilt-without-xref inference. All temporary data obey decoded/document byte limits; successful caches use their existing one-time charges. Independent stdlib MD5/RC4 known answers include generation 513 and separate user/owner authentication. This is a documented deviation from Algorithm 1.

EC3 issue 379 disallows leading zeros in reference object/generation numbers. Reported recovery preserves the numeric identity after a complete reference token is proven; ordinary integer spellings are unchanged. Braces are regular PDF characters outside Type 4 functions and therefore need no repair in names.

Nonconforming R2 revision-selector permissions use an explicit compatibility authentication path. Raw P bytes and the R2 hash/RC4 algorithms are preserved. Normal crypto authentication still rejects the selector violation; viewing recovery never guesses a password or changes access flags.

Only the CLI Unicode password path converts defined Annex D.3 code points to PDFDocEncoding for authenticated R2-R4 handlers. R5/R6 keep UTF-8. Unrepresentable input is never replaced lossily; the Document API and host protocol remain byte-oriented. The independent Euro vector covers both byte and CLI entry points.
